name: Hajib ibn Habib
bio: Hajib ibn Habib was of Asad, though the commentators differ about his exact tribe. Marzuqi makes him grandson of Khalid ibn Nadlah, of the Faq'as division.
Ode CX sets out the merits of his horse Thadiq, which the poet's wife urges him to sell.

poems.title: Ode CX: She spent the night reviling me
poems.author: Hajib ibn Habib
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Hajib son of Habib, of Asad.
poems.text:
She spent the night reviling me and pressing me to sell Thadiq, and her rebellion against me was violent.

[I said :] ' Verily thy talking in secret about Thadiq is all one to me as if it were shouted abroad ! '

She said — ' Bring help to us by selling him : I see that the price of horses has risen in the market.'

I answered — 'Knowst thou not that he is a noble horse in the attack, becoming strong for it upon but little fodder,

' A bay, built firmly and strongly as though he had drawn in his breath [and been shaped while in that condition], long in his limbs, with no superfluous flesh thereon ? '

Thou seest him bold against all other steeds, when their competitors are all broken to pieces [with exhaustion and. thirst] :

They come down with a rush like the swoop to water of the sandgrouse in 'Uman, with their spears all laid straight for the thrust.

He stretches far the rein, and never trips in his stride : compact is he in the line of the back, well covered with flesh thereon.

And I said— 'Knowst thou not that he is beautiful in all his proportions, reaching the utmost of comeliness therein ?

' He abounds in copious power to gallop when stirred by the rider's leg after an exhausting run, and it (i. e., the leg) gains the utmost of its desires from the stimulus.'

poems.title: Ode CXI: I have revealed my love for
poems.author: Hajib ibn Habib
poems.text:
I have revealed my love for Juml — what a revelation ! and her case with me has come to light after being long kept hidden ;

And tale-bearers have been busy between us, and carried their stories abroad, until I had to avoid her, though I meant not to break the bond. ($) Shall there carry me to her a fleet camel, good as a stallion, strong, bulky under the saddle, tractable, easy in hand ?

She is like a [wild ass] white in the flanks, whom an archer has driven away from the water of Mawan [by missing him] after he had him in his power ;

And he speeds swiftly through the stony deserts, [extended] like a spit of iron, while on either side of him is a cloud of dust :

The hoofs of his slightly-curved hind-legs fall on a place little liked (?), a plain of hard flat land covered with crumbling stones.

He tries for the water of Qutayyat, but it fails him, and the place where at last he finds drink is a water in Hauran :

[Daylong the waterfowl swim therein in little groups together, with eyes alert, bright like black moles on the face.]

He feared no hunter there, but plunged at once into its depths, and slaked his thirst with sweet water, no oozings of salt earth.

How noble the people whose chiefs we saw but yesterday — the best of protectors when calamities lour around !

[Our camels] pasture, watering every second day : and if they break the compact by coming down to drink the next day at noon, generous men deal gently with the transgressor's fault.

The two al-Hariths easily outstrip all others in the race to the goal, as two thoroughbred steeds keep the running entirely to themselves :

The pair deal their wealth abroad, seeking thereby fair fame : and praise is not to be bought save for a goodly price.
